The {{nihongo|'''Danbara Kofun'''|団原古墳}} is an old stone {{ill|Tomb|en|Tomb|qid=Q381885|lt=Tomb}} in the grounds of [[Nagoya Castle]] in central {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|qid=Q17|lt=Japan}}.
== History ==
The tomb is a Japanese ''[[kofun]]'', consisting of an empty stone chamber where someone originally was laid to rest. The chamber consists of roughly hewn, large slabs of stone pieced together and capped with a heavy stone roof. The entrance to the chamber was chiseled into the rock.
The kofun is located on the grounds of the Ofukemaru of Nagoya Castle.<ref>{{Cite web |title=御深井丸に佇む古代の石造物 ―団原古墳石室と河内飛鳥寺塔心礎― {{!}} イベントアーカイブ {{!}} 催し |url=https://www.nagoyajo.city.nagoya.jp/event/2023/03/20230320_4204.html |access-date=2024-11-21 |website=名古屋城公式ウェブサイト |language=ja}}</ref> In 1988, experts were able to determine that the tomb must have originally come from what is today {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|en|Shimane Prefecture|qid=Q132751|lt=Shimane Prefecture}}, or ancient {{ill|Izumo Province|en|Izumo Province|qid=Q582846|lt=Izumo Province}}. The exact original location of the tomb cannot however be determined since most of the areas in question are today used for agriculture. Shimane Prefecture is about 500 kilometres to the west of Nagoya. How and when the tomb was transported to Nagoya Castle and what purpose it served there is unknown. It could be that the tomb was reused as a storage chamber, however that remains speculation.{{Citation needed|date=May 2012}}
